title: Level 4 (Expert) - C-14
notes:
West leads the ♦4 against 7NT. West's lead is won by South. South must find the ♣Q for his thirteenth trick (4 spades, 3 hearts, 3 diamonds, and the ♣A and ♣K will make up South's other 12 tricks).

South should cash his spade, heart, and diamond tricks before playing clubs. It may be possible to get enough of a count on the hand to know how to play clubs. On the above layout, for example, West will show up with 4 spades, 5 hearts, and at least 3 diamonds. West can have no more than 1 club and East can be finessed for the ♣Q with certainty.

On the above layout, West will count out to 3 spades, 5 hearts, and at least 3 diamonds. There is no certain play as West might have a doubleton ♣Q. However, the odds heavily favour playing East for the ♣Q as he is known to hold at least 5 clubs.

On the actual layout, West will be known to have 4 spades, 2 hearts, and at least 3 diamonds (9 known cards). East will be known to have 1 spade, 5 hearts, and at least 3 diamonds (also 9 known cards). It seems like South's play in clubs is a complete guess.

South can solve this problem with an unusual application of the Principle of Restricted Choice. West led from a suit with 3 or 4 small cards. If West had a similar holding in clubs, he may have led that suit instead. West should thus be played for the ♣Q.
